## Context / Problem

A worktree's editable install writes the project version into its `.dist-info` once, at
install time. Rebasing onto a `main` that bumped the version leaves it stale, so
`importlib.metadata.version("nava-rebar")` — and `rebar.__version__`
(`src/rebar/__init__.py:144`) — report the old version while `pyproject.toml` declares
the new one. Nothing warns. It surfaces ~40 minutes into `make verify` as public-API
surface drift on `rebar.__version__` (`tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py:78`, `:83`),
and `scripts/gen_api_surface.py` `_check()` (lines 230-248) advises
`python scripts/gen_api_surface.py --update`, which would commit the stale version into
`tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json`. It cost a 42-minute run on `19ba-bd62-1adb-41df`
and recurred on `a018-a2c0-fc15-434c`. Reproduced independently on 2026-10-31 across
`c9159d2af47` (0.13.1 -> 0.14.0); evidence is in this ticket's comments, including that
`--update` in the stale env rewrites the baseline to `0.13.1`, that `docs/releasing.md`
step 1 (`uv lock` then `--update`, no reinstall) has the same trap, and that a fake
`nava_rebar-0.0.1.dist-info` on `PYTHONPATH` reproduces the mismatch hermetically.

## Approach

Follow the existing pattern for an environment precondition: `tests/conftest.py:173`
`pytest_configure` calls `floor_violation()` from `tests/_git_floor.py` and raises
`pytest.UsageError`; `_select_repo_pandoc` in the same file loads a `scripts/` module
by path with `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`.

1. **Detector in the gate script.** Add
   `installed_version_drift(*, installed=None, declared=None) -> str | None` to
   `scripts/gen_api_surface.py` (stdlib only). Declared = `pyproject.toml`
   `[project].version` via `tomllib`; installed = `importlib.metadata.version("nava-rebar")`.
   Return `None` when equal, when the distribution is not installed
   (`PackageNotFoundError`, matching the source-tree fallback at
   `src/rebar/__init__.py:146`), or when there is no static version. Otherwise return a
   diagnostic naming both versions, `make install` as the remedy, and "do not regenerate
   the baseline". Keyword overrides mirror `floor_violation(installed=..., floor=...)`.
2. **Fail the pytest session up front.** In `pytest_configure`, beside the git-floor
   check, load `scripts/gen_api_surface.py` by path and raise `pytest.UsageError` with
   the diagnostic. This precedes collection, so it runs before the surface gate under
   `make test`, `make verify` and bare `pytest`. Aligned environments (all CI, which
   installs fresh with `uv sync --locked`) see no change.
3. **Correct the gate's advice.** In `_check()`, write the diagnostic when there is a
   mismatch, and omit the `--update` line when the only drift is
   `~ CHANGED  rebar.__version__`. Other drift keeps the existing `--update` text.
4. **Refuse to write the corruption.** `main(["--update"])` (lines 262-264) exits 2 with
   the diagnostic and leaves the baseline untouched on a mismatch. This covers the
   release path, which has no pytest session in front of it.
5. **Docs.** `AGENTS.md`: one sentence in the Git-workflow worktree bullet — run
   `make install` after any rebase that crosses a version bump. `docs/releasing.md`
   step 1: run `make install` after `uv lock` and before `--update`, with the reason.

Rejected: a Makefile-only preflight (misses bare `pytest`); reinstalling from conftest
(mutates the venv from a test run); dropping `__version__` from the baseline (a
separate policy change that removes release-bump coverage).

## Scope

- `scripts/gen_api_surface.py` — detector, `_check()` text, `--update` refusal.
- `tests/conftest.py` — `pytest_configure` precondition.
- `tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py` — new tests.
- `AGENTS.md` — one sentence.
- `docs/releasing.md` — reinstall before `--update`.

## Testing

In `tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py`:

- Detector: `installed="0.13.1", declared="0.14.0"` returns text with both versions and
  `make install`; equal versions return `None`; a missing distribution returns `None`;
  no overrides in the test env returns `None`.
- End-to-end with a tmp fake `nava_rebar-0.0.1.dist-info` prepended to `PYTHONPATH`
  (no venv mutation):
  - `python -m pytest --collect-only -q tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py` exits 4
    (usage error) and its output names both versions and `make install`.
  - `python scripts/gen_api_surface.py --check` exits 1; stderr names `make install` and
    does not contain `gen_api_surface.py --update`.
  - `python scripts/gen_api_surface.py --update` exits 2 and the committed baseline's
    bytes are unchanged (read before and after).
- Aligned: existing `test_committed_baseline_matches_live_surface` and
  `test_default_invocation_runs_the_check` stay green.
- Red-before-fix: new tests run against the unmodified script/conftest; failures
  recorded as a ticket comment.

Commands: `pytest tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py`, `make lint`, `make typecheck`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: With an installed `nava-rebar` version differing from `pyproject.toml`, a
      message naming both versions and `make install` is reported before the surface
      gate runs — `pytest --collect-only` exits 4 with that text (shadow test).
- [ ] AC2: With matching versions, no such message is emitted and existing behaviour is
      unchanged — existing surface-gate tests pass and the detector returns `None`.
- [ ] AC3: When the only surface drift is `rebar.__version__` and versions disagree, the
      `--check` failure text does not recommend `gen_api_surface.py --update` (shadow test).
- [ ] AC4: `grep -n "crosses a version bump" AGENTS.md` finds the `make install` rule.
- [ ] AC5: The new tests cover AC1-AC3 and AC6 and were red before the fix (comment).
- [ ] AC6: On a mismatch `gen_api_surface.py --update` exits 2 and leaves the baseline
      byte-identical (test); `docs/releasing.md` step 1 runs `make install` before
      `--update` (grep).
- [ ] AC7: `pytest tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py`, `make lint` and `make typecheck`
      pass, and the Gerrit change carries `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.
